It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data , and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record. more…

articles.body: 요약: 2026년 국내 AI 기업 11개사가 허깅페이스에 공개한 언어모델 174개의 다운로드를 분석했다. 직전 30일 136만 회 중 82.2%, 올해 누적 666만 회 중 58.0%가 비드래프트 모델이고, 30일 상위 5개 모델은 모두 GGUF·NVFP4 압축 형태다. 올해 국내 AI 기업들은 앞다퉈 자체 모델을 허깅페이스에 공개했다. 세계 개발자들은 그중 어떤 모델을 실제로 내려받았을까. 2026년 1월 1일 이후 공개된 모델만 놓고, 국내 대표 AI 기업 11개사의 다운로드를 직전 30일과 올해 누적으로 나눠 분석했다. 분석 대상은 LG AI연구원, SK텔레콤, 업스테이지, 모티프테크놀로지스, 비드래프트, 네이버, 카카오, 엔씨소프트(NC AI), KT, 크래프톤, 트릴리온랩스의 공식 허깅페이스 계정이다. 기준은 하나다. 개발사가 자기 공식 계정으로 직접 공개한 언어모델만 센다. 다른 개발사 모델을 원래 이름 그대로 다시 올린 변환본과 해외·개인 재배포본은 넣지 않았고, 이 규칙은 모든 회사에 똑같이 적용했다. 수치는 2026년 11월 16일 허깅페이스 공개 API 실측값이며, 글로벌 LLM 다운로드 리더보드 한국 탭의 「11개사 2026 분석」, 「2026년 출시」 보기에서 같은 숫자를 매일 확인할 수 있다.

articles.title: One Query, Six Ranked Lists, One Answer: Tuning Rank Fusion for Multilingual Search
articles.excerpt: How one constant in Reciprocal Rank Fusion lets a confident top match stand out — and why the right value depends on how correlated your retrievers are. When you type a query into SpotRecall, my priva…
articles.body: How one constant in Reciprocal Rank Fusion lets a confident top match stand out — and why the right value depends on how correlated your retrievers are. When you type a query into SpotRecall, my private on-device browser recall extension, it does not run one search. It runs six. The query is first searched as typed. Then Chrome's on-device Translator turns it into the other two languages SpotRecall covers — English, Japanese, and Chinese — because, as I wrote earlier in this series, translating the query beats shipping a model four times larger. Each of those three variants is searched twice: once by BM25 keyword search and once by a small multilingual embedding model ( multilingual-e5-small , int8, running locally). Three variants times two retrievers gives six ranked lists.

articles.title: When I tell Cursor "just make it work", this rule stops the shortcut from rotting
articles.excerpt: Cursor is very obedient about the word "quick." If I say "just make it work," it will often make something work by skipping the parts that are annoying: the ownership check, the empty state, the test,…
articles.body: Cursor is very obedient about the word "quick." If I say "just make it work," it will often make something work by skipping the parts that are annoying: the ownership check, the empty state, the test, the rollback. The feature looks done. A week later I cannot remember which of those shortcuts is load-bearing, and one of them is in a path real users hit. I got tired of cleaning that up, so I stopped treating "MVP" as a quality setting. I treat it as a scope setting. The rule lives in .cursor/rules/ and I pull it in when I hear myself say "hack this in," "just for now," or "we'll tidy it later." Cut scope, not quality The useful question is not "how do we write this faster?" It is "what can we not build yet?" I tell the agent to cut these first: A settings screen.

articles.title: How do you architect robust Playwright E2E tests to validate coordinated UI state consistency across multiple, interconn
articles.excerpt: 🔥 Playwright Alert: Is your SPA's UI consistency causing flaky E2E tests? ⚠️ 90% of engineers struggle to reliably validate complex, coordinated UI state across multiple components in Playwright. Her…
articles.body: 🔥 Playwright Alert: Is your SPA's UI consistency causing flaky E2E tests? ⚠️ 90% of engineers struggle to reliably validate complex, coordinated UI state across multiple components in Playwright. Here's how to master it. 📌 Problem Statement In sophisticated Single-Page Applications (SPAs), especially dashboards, user actions or backend pushes trigger cascaded, asynchronous UI updates across interconnected components. Traditional Playwright assertions, focused on individual elements, often lead to flakiness due to race conditions or partial updates. The real challenge is verifying the entire coordinated state is consistent and stable, not just isolated elements. ❌ Relying on page.waitForTimeout() or isolated assertions makes tests brittle.

articles.body: How real container images, security checks, and CI failures helped improve the InfraPulse security pipeline. In Part 1 — 12 Green CI Jobs, 422 Security Findings , I shared an important lesson: even when all required CI checks pass, security scanners can still report hundreds of findings that need further investigation. In Part 2 — From 422 Security Findings to Auditable Evidence , I explored how InfraPulse evolved to produce more reliable evidence about software components, artifact integrity, and the software supply chain. Now, in Part 3, a new challenge emerged: How can we make sure these security checks still work when we move beyond controlled tests and start analyzing real container images?

articles.title: Exposing ThingsDB as a MySQL Database
articles.excerpt: Integrating a high-speed, object-oriented database with traditional reporting tools, BI dashboards, or legacy applications often hits a familiar roadblock: most external tools expect SQL. With the new…
articles.body: Integrating a high-speed, object-oriented database with traditional reporting tools, BI dashboards, or legacy applications often hits a familiar roadblock: most external tools expect SQL. With the new MySQL Endpoint module ( module-go-mysqlendpoint ), ThingsDB can now speak the MySQL wire protocol directly. This allows you to connect standard MySQL clients, BI tools (like Grafana, Metabase, or Power BI), and existing SQL drivers straight to your ThingsDB collections, no ETL pipelines or data duplication required. High Availability Out of the Box Because ThingsDB modules run across every node in your cluster, the MySQL endpoint is automatically available on all ThingsDB nodes .

articles.title: NASA's interstellar Voyager 1 probe is about to reach 1 light-day from Earth after nearly 50 years in space
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth. NASA's long-running interstellar Voyager 1 probe will mark one light-day of distance from Earth on Nov. 18, when the spacecraft is 49 years, two months and 11 days old. The agency recently stated the record distance, which will be reached at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (101607 GMT) is "a huge milestone by any measure, and a day worth celebrating." During the light-day crossover, Voyager will be in contact with the Madrid station of the three-antenna Deep Space Network that monitors all deep-space missions. The spacecraft is currently making its way through the constellation Ophiuchus from the perspective of Earth, said Jeffrey Hayes, a NASA official whose work includes Voyager 1.
